details.description: Claude Mythos 5.1 is Anthropic's invitation-only model for vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations, released September 1, 2026 through Anthropic's Project Glasswing. It shares its underlying model, 1-million-token context window, and 128,000-token max output with the publicly available Claude Fable 5.1, but runs with more permissive safeguards for defensive security research and biology work. Anthropic describes it as the strongest cyber-capable model it has released to date, while stating it still falls within the lower risk category of its Frontier Compliance Framework.
advantages: Anthropic states it demonstrates the strongest cyber capabilities of any model it has released, while still falling within the lower risk category of its Frontier Compliance Framework (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).
Scores 60.9% on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 agentic-coding benchmark, ahead of the 55.8% Anthropic reports for Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).

Anthropic reports designing protein binders with binding affinities up to 10 times higher than the best entries in Adaptyv Bio's protein design competitions across three targets (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).
Anthropic reports a hit rate of nearly 50% across 12 protein-design targets, compared with the 10-15% it says is typical today (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).

Anthropic reports optimizing seven open-source biology deep-learning models for up to 2.5x faster inference, cutting estimated GPU costs by 30-60% on genome-wide analyses (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).
Supports a 1-million-token context window with always-on adaptive thinking and 128,000 max output tokens (Claude Mythos 5.1 model overview).
disadvantages: Available only by invitation through Anthropic's Project Glasswing, limited to vetted US cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations (Claude Mythos 5.1 model overview).

Anthropic's own documentation recommends starting with Claude Opus 5 for most workloads and reserving this model tier for demanding reasoning or long-horizon agentic work (Claude Fable 5.1 what's new documentation).
Even for approved users, Anthropic still restricts penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability scanning (Anthropic Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 announcement).
Reliable knowledge cutoff of June 2026 (Claude Mythos 5.1 model overview).
use_cases: Defensive cybersecurity vulnerability research for organizations vetted through the Cyber Verification Program
Biology and life-sciences research such as protein design, via the Life Sciences Verification Program
Long-running agentic coding across large codebases and multi-hour sessions
Multistep research and analysis, and building documents, spreadsheets, and slides
Powers Anthropic's own Claude Security vulnerability-scanning product

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1

notes: Catalog facts (1M max input tokens, 128K max output tokens, image_input + text_input + text_output modality, anthropic/bedrock providers, no deprecation date) match Anthropic's Mythos 5.1 model-overview page (1M context, 128K output, 'Text and images -> text') and its model-deprecations table (Active, invite only, tentative retirement not sooner than September 1, 2027). Mythos 5.1 is not an openly purchasable API model: Anthropic offers it only to Project Glasswing participants vetted through its Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program, which is unusual for a catalog entry and is called out in disadvantages since it directly affects who can use it. The full system-card PDF (with additional safety-evaluation detail) exceeded the size this tool can fetch.
